chunks: As for what Saʿd ibn ʿAbd Allah narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Husayn, from Faḍālah, from Sayf ibn ʿUmayrah, from Abū Bakr al-Ḥaḍramī, who said:

I prayed al-Maghrib with my companions, and when I had prayed two rakʿahs, I said the salām. Some of them said, “You only prayed two rakʿahs,” so I repeated it. Then I informed Abū ʿAbd Allah عليه السلام, and he said, “Perhaps you repeated it?” I said, “Yes.” So he laughed, then said, “It is only sufficient for you to stand and perform one rakʿah.” Indeed, the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم forgot and gave salām after two rakʿahs, then he mentioned the hadith of Dhū al-Shimālayn. He said: then he stood and added two rakʿahs to it.”

key_terms.أَعَدْتُ: I repeated the prayer from the beginning
key_terms.ذِي الشِّمَالَيْنِ: Dhū al-Shimālayn, the person mentioned in the well-known report about forgetfulness in prayer
key_terms.رَكْعَةً: one additional unit needed to complete the prayer
key_terms.رَكْعَتَيْنِ: two units of prayer performed before the mistake was noticed
key_terms.سَلَّمْتُ: I gave the salām ending the prayer
key_terms.سَهَا: he forgot or made an unintentional mistake in prayer

ai.seo_question: What should a person do if they accidentally give salām after two rakʿahs in al-Maghrib prayer?
ai.summary: This hadith discusses forgetfulness in salat (prayer), specifically in al-Maghrib prayer when one gives salām after only two rakʿahs. Imam al-Sadiq عليه السلام explains that the prayer does not need to be repeated entirely; rather, one should stand and complete the missing rakʿah. The report also cites the precedent of the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم completing the prayer after an unintended early salām.
